tone_statements.citation: Raen, Konstanse. 1993. Les activités du centre de littérature pere. In: Adala, Hermenegildo & Boutrais, Jean (eds.), Peuples et cultures de l'Adamaoua (Cameroun): actes du colloque de Ngaoundéré du 14 au 16 janvier 1992, 225-234. Paris: ORSTOM / Ngaoundéré-Anthropos (Colloques et Séminaires). ISBN 2-7099-1167-1.
tone_statements.quote: Le ton est significatif en pere. On trouve beaucoup de paires minimales où la seule différence entre les mots réside dans le ton. On compte trois tons distinctifs, même si l'on peut compter plusieurs hauteurs phonétiquement. [...] Le ton se manifeste sur les syllabes, c'est-à-dire que chaque syllabe a son propre ton, et doit toujours se prononcer à voix haute, moyenne ou basse. [...] Le ton n'est pas seulement important pour distinguer les différents mots, mais aussi pour exprimer des distinctions grammaticales, par exemple la distinction transitive-intransitive dans un groupe de verbes
tone_statements.translation: Tone is significant in Pere. There are many minimal pairs in which the only difference between the words lies in the tone. There are three distinctive tones, even if more pitch levels can be counted phonetically. [...] Tone is realised on the syllables, i.e. each syllable has its own tone and must always be pronounced at high, mid or low pitch. [...] Tone is important not only for distinguishing different words but also for expressing grammatical distinctions, for example the transitive-intransitive distinction in a group of verbs
tone_statements.locator: p. 228, section 'Les tons' (continued p. 229: reflexive-reciprocal by tone change on the root); orthography summary pp. 227-228
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (high, mid, low) contrasting on every syllable (syllable = TBU), with lexical minimal pairs and grammatical functions (transitive/intransitive verb pairs, reflexive-reciprocal by root tone change, tonally distinguished pronouns); contours arise in compounds and as a predictable low-mid glide on CVN syllables.

sources.citation: Kastenholz, Raimund. 2020. Coverbs and auxiliaries in Pèdè. Language in Africa 1(3): 353-372. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-353-372
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Confirms a three-level tone language: completive suffix has low/mid/high tonal allomorphs by transitivity (p. 356); low-tone transitive vs high-tone intransitive verb pairs (fn. 16, p. 364); 'All verb stems, including coverbs, and auxiliaries, receive a high tone marking as part of a verbal noun' (fn. 22, p. 367). States p. 354: 'Pèdè is a notoriously understudied language. With the exception of Kastenholz (2011; 2018), only pedagogical materials (e.g. Raen 1981, among others) are accessible.' Data = Almé variety.

sources.note: A literacy-centre report that summarises the phonological basis of the Pere orthography (from Raen 1981): 21 consonants, 7 short/6 long oral vowels, nasal vowels, 7 diphthongs, then a dedicated section 'Les tons' (p. 228-229): tone is lexically distinctive with many minimal pairs; three distinctive tones (high, mid, low) illustrated on a verb triplet ('il aime / il traverse / il partage'); the syllable is the tone-bearing unit; exceptions explained by intonation; compound nouns may carry a contour ('ton modulé'); CVN syllables have a predictable low-mid (3-2) glide written as low (gɛ̀ni 'le c…
